name: Millhaven storehouse and mill
region: Millhaven, near side of the bridge
chapter4Note: Referenced only, in Jaina's memory when she enters the sick village's granary: 'the storehouse by the bridge, the loudest place in that whole dead village'; she had told Sylvanas 'a store is where things end up. Here was where it ended up.' Reinterprets the Ch3 read as a sink in a grain-supply chain without confirming Millhaven's storehouse was supplied by the same man.

sensoryProfile.sight: A stone storehouse with a slate roof and a cart-wide door beside the mill; pale grain dust in a slow gold fog under the lantern; sacks stacked shoulder-high, each chalk-tallied along the seam in rows of five struck through; a bin of loose grain open by the door with a wooden scoop standing up out of the heap; a tally board on a nail above it with the last line half-written. The mill wheel stands still, dripping, green weed furring the paddles; the race pours white beneath the arch.
sensoryProfile.sound: The crystal rattling in its claws 'like a beetle in a box'; the race.
sensoryProfile.touch: Dust soft as ash; frost spreads across the boards, the dust taking it and going grey.
sensoryProfile.atmosphere: The loudest place in Millhaven; looks like a place where someone was in the middle of filling sacks.

establishedFacts.fact: The mage reads the storehouse as the loudest place in Millhaven, louder than the crossing, but refuses to call it the origin: 'a store is where things end up'. Sylvanas does not argue.
A far door was propped open with a sack to give Sylvanas a clean line through the building to the water.
The mill wheel stands still, dripping, with weed on the paddles; the race still runs under the arch of the bridge.

eventsHere.event: Jaina's left-hand storehouse read: the loudest place in Millhaven; skin left on the boards; Sylvanas bans further hand-reads that night.
